title: handoff (Builder -> Critic, one per turn)
description: The Builder's steering input to the Critic. It is NOT a summary of what was done - it is a set of pointed requests aimed at what a green gate structurally cannot see. A vague handoff buys a useless review and wastes a turn.

tests_added.description: MANDATORY and complete. Every test written or changed this turn, with the case it proves and whether it was observed failing first. A test added without a red observation has not been shown to be wired to anything, and saying so here is cheaper than having the Critic find it.

why_not_red.description: Required when was_red_first is false. The honest reason - not an excuse, just the reason.

verification_requests.description: Concrete asks pointing at what the gate cannot see. 'Check the tests' is worthless - they already ran. 'The empty-input test asserts equal(result, "") but the stub also returned ""; confirm it would fail against a wrong implementation' is the shape.

known_gaps.description: The honesty channel. A gap disclosed here is weighed far more leniently than the same gap found by the Critic.

shortcuts_taken.description: Any skip, focus, suppression, disabled check or loosened assertion introduced this turn, with its justification. Leaving one out is a trust violation rather than an oversight: these are precisely the moves that make a green run meaningless, and the integrity leg will find them anyway.

builder_self_verdict.description: pass only when the Builder believes the contract is fully met. Termination needs this AND two consecutive Critic passes AND the orchestrator's matrix GREEN on the same turn.
